newsitem.title: GERMANY: MG near deal with former CEO - report.
newsitem.headline: MG near deal with former CEO - report.

text.p: German industrial group Metallgesellschaft AG (MG) is close to a settlement with its previous chief executive and finance officer, putting an end to events that nearly drove the firm to collapse in 1993, a newspaper report said on Saturday.

According to a report in the weekly Welt am Sonntag newspaper released ahead of publication on Sunday, the MG supervisory board is to meet on January 31 to discuss a settlement for former chairman Heinz Schimmelbusch and finance director Meinhard Forster.

The report said MG was now prepared to accept an out-of-court settlement with Schimmelbusch that would guarantee his pension of 340,000 marks from the age of 65 and assume all of his legal fees resulting from the company's suit for damages against the former chief executive.
MG was not immediately available for comment.

The company last year rejected a settlement for the two former officials, who were blamed for huge losses that threatened the company's existence in 1993 as a result of dubious oil dealings in the United States.

But, according to the the newspaper report, the supervisory board is now expected to accept a settlement plan because it wants shareholders to be able to give their approval at the annual general meeting in Frankfurt on March 27.
The company must decide on an out-of-court settlement by April 30, when a Frankfurt court is due to begin hearings in the damages suit MG filed against Schimmelbusch.
